attributes.context: This is part of Article 55, Technological Changes. Section 143 states that automated equipment and technology is available in the retail food industry, that the Employer seeks to preserve work opportunities, and that the Union recognizes the Employer's right to use modern technology.

extraction_text:
Section 144. In the event the Employer introduces major technological changes which, for the purpose of this Article, are defined as price marking and electronic scanners and which would have a direct material impact affecting bargaining unit work, thirty (30) days advance notice of such change will be given to the Union.

In addition, the Employer agrees:

1. Any retraining necessary will be furnished by the Employer at no expense to the employees.

2. Where retraining is not applicable the Employer will make every effort to effect a transfer to another store, or other employment.

attributes.context: The severance obligation is tied to Section 144's definition of major technological changes as price marking and electronic scanners and to the preceding requirements that the Employer provide retraining or make efforts to transfer employees.

extraction_text:
3. In the event the employee is not retrained or transferred and is permanently displaced as a direct result of major technological changes as defined above, the employee will be eligible for severance pay in accordance with the following provisions:

a) All employees, excluding courtesy clerks, with two (2) or more years of continuous service will be eligible for one (1) week's severance pay for each year of continuous service. Maximum severance pay of ten (10) weeks' pay to be paid on a lump sum basis. Weekly severance pay shall be determined by the average number of hours worked for the four (4) weeks preceding displacement, not to exceed forty (40) hours' straight-time pay.

b) An employee shall be disqualified from severance pay in the event the employee:

(1) Refuses retraining,

(2) Refuses a transfer or other employment within a radius of forty (40) miles

(3) Voluntarily terminates employment.

attributes.context: This provision appears in Letter of Agreement #16 between UFCW Local 7 and King Soopers, Inc., dated 9/24/90, and the chunk states that the Company will provide the Union a copy of the current ACTMEDIA work contract and the agreement expires concurrent with that contract unless mutually continued.

extraction_text:
WHEREAS, King Soopers, Inc., has contracted certain services with ACTMEDIA, Inc.; and WHEREAS, this work would not normally otherwise exist within stores; NOW, THEREFORE, the parties identified above agree as follows:

1. Representatives from ACTMEDIA, Inc., may maintain advertising pace on aisle vision billboards, shopping carts and the shelf talker instant coupon machine in all stores, with the understanding that such advertising placards are not to include pricing of any kind.

2. It is further understood that this work is strictly limited as set forth above and shall not be expanded further.

attributes.context: This appears in Article 55, Technological Changes, Section 143, which recognizes that automated equipment and technology is available for the retail food industry and that the parties share the objective of protecting work opportunities while the Employer avails itself of modern technology.

extraction_text: At the same time, the Union recognizes that the Employer has a right to avail itself of modern technology.

attributes.context: Appears in Article 6, Rights of Management, immediately after Section 14, which reserves the Employer's general rights to manage the store, direct working forces, and make reasonable rules and regulations.

extraction_text: Section 15. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to prevent the Employer from placing cash registers in the Deli Department of the store and from assigning the employees of such department to operate the register.
